newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Farmers say Tanzania government neglects coffee.
newsitem.headline: Farmers say Tanzania government neglects coffee.

text.p: Traders and growers in Tanzania's key northern coffee region say the government is neglecting them and driving out young farmers.
"The young generation is not interested in coffee production because to them it doesn't pay," a long-established local trader told Reuters. "We rarely see anyone from the government here.
"The chemicals required for fighting diseases are so expensive and the farmers cannot afford it. They have the will to put in more efforts, but they are lacking the funds."
He said farmers needed advice at all stages of processing, including financial assistance to purchase seedlings and the introduction of new disease-resistant varieties.

"The quality can only be improved by involving more people to teach the farmers how to process the coffee right after the berries have been picked -- until drying," he said. "Coffee should be washed in clean water. And they (farmers) must be told when to spray against diseases and at the right time."

Small steps have already been taken. Last August the government launched a grower-education project involving 30 experts from the ministry of agriculture advising smallholders on farming techniques, farmers and coffee officials said.

Despite the current problems, it was agreed that Tanzania would become an important player on the world market if an intensive replanting programme was implemented and processing quality was further improved.
"It is going to take a while, three or five years minimum before you see significant changes, but I'm very optimistic," said one farmer.
